title: Switching from upright alto to trombone
summary: A missing trombonist in Pansy Lane's band led him to try the slide; positions came naturally.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well, how did you learn to play so wonderfully? I mean, you not only have a wonderful ear and wonderful tone, but even your position. I mean, you got around...

Well, Pansy Lane, that's Papa Lane's son. His name is Alfred. They called him Pansy. He played the trumpet and his brother-in-law, Leon Smello. I was playing the upright alto and he was playing the trombone. So he got under the weather one time and he didn't show up. And, uh, we were playing down at Crescent City Carnival Club. And, uh, Pansy says, uh, geez, what are we going to do for a trombone? He says, I said, well, I can play the trombone parts on the alto. He says, why don't you try the trombone, Bruno? So that's when that song was out, How Dry I Am, Now I Am. So I put the trombone again and I started blowing and I liked it. Slide. And then I was thinking all the time of my brother Henny, you know, I said, oh, I could never be that way. So we played and I played that. I did a lot of guesswork, you know, it was new to me. So from that time on, I liked trombone. I threw the alto. The alto was what, uh, what's his name, was playing with Bobby Hackett today, uh, Kerry. That's the horn I used to play for the Mardi Gras parade.
Now, Monk Hazel still uses a...
Well, that's a French horn. Yeah, he uses the ground. Well, it's an alto, but it's a French alto, a mellophone.
Um, did you watch your brother? Is that where you got a lot of ideas?
No, I used to drew when that guy played. I wanted to throw that trombone in the hat rack.
But there never was anybody that actually showed you where the seven positions were? Nothing.
Did you even think about whether you're going in the fourth position or the third or anything? I feel it. You don't even think about that position?
My heart puts my arm there.
Where to put a smear, where to put the right notes. Yeah. It's all done by ear and heart.
